title: Prove the gpg-hang defense with a signing fixture and harden the worktree merge commit the same way
action: Review B-P1-2: the close bookkeeping commit's --no-gpg-sign and stdin-null defenses have zero assertions (deleting either keeps 1461 tests green) and the fixture masks the condition by forcing gpgsign false; the SAME hazard is still live un-hardened in worktree merge's commit (phases.rs:358 via the shared run_git in worktree/git.rs, which sets no stdin and no signing flag) - and that path holds the worktree-admin lock mid-merge. Fix: (1) close.rs: add a test that sets commit.gpgsign=true AND gpg.program pointing at a stub that exits 1 in the fixture repo, then asserts the bookkeeping commit still lands green - this is the pin that fails if --no-gpg-sign is removed; remove or repurpose the masking gpgsign=false fixture line where it hides the condition. (2) worktree/git.rs run_git: spawn with stdin Stdio::null(). (3) phases.rs merge commit: add --no-gpg-sign to the commit args. (4) same stub-proof test on the merge path: a merge-commit fixture with gpgsign=true + failing gpg stub proving the merge commit lands. Keep every existing test green; wording of failure texts unchanged (the R81 spelling drift is a separate P2, do not touch it here).

truths: removing --no-gpg-sign from the close bookkeeping commit turns a test red
worktree merge's commit carries --no-gpg-sign and run_git spawns with stdin null
a gpgsign=true repo with a failing gpg stub closes AND merges green

artifacts.substantive: stdin-null runner + merge-path hardening plus stub-proof tests

trace.outcome: gpg-hang defense proven by failing-signer stubs on BOTH paths (red when flag removed); run_git stdin null; merge commit --no-gpg-sign; masking fixture line retired
